extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or advanced undergraduates studying algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's Foundations of Algebraic Geometry)
extracted.subtask_description: Define and construct the relative Spec and Proj of quasicoherent (graded) sheaves of algebras on a scheme; use these to characterize affine and projective morphisms and to study relative notions of ampleness, base-change, and projectivization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Spec – universal property
rubrics_metrics.description: Spec of a quasicoherent sheaf of algebras B on X (β: Spec B → X) is defined by the universal property that X-morphisms W → Spec B (over X, with µ:W→X) are in bijection with OX-algebra maps α: B → µ_* O_W (functorially in W).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence is unique up to unique isomorphism when it exists; it can be computed affine-locally (over Spec A, Spec B is the usual Spec of the algebra Γ(Spec A,B)). Behavior under base change: Spec commutes with base change (Exercise 17.1.F). Proposition 17.1.3: restriction to open subsets satisfies the corresponding universal property. There is an isomorphism φ: B ≃ β_* O_{Spec B}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine morphism characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism µ: Z → X is affine iff Z ≅ Spec µ_* O_Z as an X-scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus every affine morphism can be recovered via the Spec construction; conversely, Spec B → X is affine. (See Exercise 17.1.D.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Total space / vector bundle as Spec Sym•(F∨)
rubrics_metrics.description: The total space of a finite-rank locally free sheaf F is Spec(Sym• F∨), which is a rank n vector bundle (denoted A^n_X when F ≅ O_X^{⊕n}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show fibers are A^n and F is recovered as the sheaf of sections of the total space. Beware dualization conventions: some authors take Spec(Sym• F) as the associated bundle. Construction behaves well under base change (Exercise 17.1.G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Proj – gluing construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a quasicoherent Z_{≥0}-graded sheaf of algebras S• on X satisfying reasonable hypotheses, glue the ordinary Proj constructions over affine opens to form Proj_X S• with structure morphism β: Proj_X S• → X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction via gluing data (Exercise 17.2.B and 17.2.C). Over each affine open Spec A the preimage is computed by the usual Proj_A S•(Spec A). One may also formulate a universal property (see Stacks tag 01NS), but the text takes a more pedestrian gluing approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypotheses 17.2.1: finite generation in degree 1
rubrics_metrics.description: For usefulness of Proj, require S• to be generated in degree 1 and S1 to be finite type; precisely the natural map Sym•_{OX} S1 → S• should be surjective, checked affine-locally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These hypotheses will be enforced in the rest of the book for Proj constructions; one can relax the 'degree 1 generation' condition if needed. Many subsequent results assume these hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: O(1) on Proj under degree-1 hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: If S• is finitely generated in degree 1, one can construct an invertible sheaf O_{Proj S•}(1) on Proj S• restricting to the usual O(1) on each affine piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for relating Proj to very ample line bundles and projectivity (Exercise 17.2.D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proj commutes with base change (affine case and general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proj construction is compatible with base change: Proj_B(S• ⊗_A B) ≃ (Proj_A S•) ×_{Spec A} Spec B (Exercise 17.2.A), and more generally (Proj ρ^* S•) ≃ Z ×_X Proj_X S• for any ρ: Z → X (Exercise 17.2.E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also O(1) behaves compatibly under base change: O_{Proj_B(...)}(1) ≃ α^* γ^* O_{Proj_A S•}(1) in the diagram given in Exercise 17.2.A. Base-change compatibility underlies many preservation properties of projectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of π-very ample (relative very ampleness)
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is proper and L an invertible sheaf on X, L is π-very ample (π-very ample) if X ≅ Proj_Y S• with L ≃ O(1) for some S• satisfying finite generation in degree 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the relative analog of very ample; definition depends on existence of a Proj presentation. See 17.2.2 and Exercise 17.3.A for useful characterizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of projective morphism
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism π: X → Y is projective if there is an isomorphism X ≃ Proj_Y S• for some quasicoherent graded O_Y-algebra S• satisfying the finite generation-in-degree-1 hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This generalizes projective A-schemes. Warnings: O(1) is not part of Grothendieck's definition (though one might prefer it); projectivity is preserved by base change but not obviously affine-local on the base without additional data/Noetherian hypotheses (17.3.1 and warnings). Hartshorne's definition differs but agrees in nice cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of projective morphisms (closed embedding into projective bundle)
rubrics_metrics.description: π is projective with O(1) ≃ L iff there exist a finite-type quasicoherent sheaf S1 on Y and a closed embedding i: X ↪ P_{S1} over Y with i^* O_{P_{S1}}(1) ≃ L. If Y admits an ample line bundle M, π is projective iff X embeds as a closed subscheme of P^n_Y for some n (Exercise 17.3.A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a practical criterion to check projectivity by embedding into projective bundles; use finite generation of S1 and twisting by powers of an ample line bundle to obtain global generation (hints refer to Theorem 16.6.2 and Exercise 17.2.G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiprojective morphisms (relative)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Y is quasicompact, π: X → Y is quasiprojective if it can be expressed as a quasicompact open embedding into a scheme projective over Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The general definition is more delicate (EGA), but this suffices here; the notion will not be used heavily in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation properties of projective morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Projective morphisms are preserved by base change and (under hypotheses) by composition: they are proper (hence separated, finite type, universally closed), and composition is projective when the final target is quasicompact (Exercise 17.3.B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs rely on Proj base-change (17.2.E) and embeddings into projective bundles. There are cautions about locality and composition in general; see Caution 17.3.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite morphisms are projective
rubrics_metrics.description: Finite morphisms Z → X are projective: one can construct a graded sheaf S• with S0 ≃ OX and Sn ≃ B (for n>0) where Z ≃ Spec B, giving Z ≃ Proj S• (Exercise 17.3.D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular closed embeddings are projective. Thus closed embedding ⇒ finite ⇒ projective ⇒ proper (chain of implications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative global generation / base-point-freeness
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y quasicompact quasiseparated and F a quasicoherent sheaf on X, F is relatively globally generated (w.r.t. π) if the natural map π^* π_* F → F is surjective. A locally free L is relatively base-point-free if it is relatively globally generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quasicompactness and quasiseparatedness ensure π_* F is quasicoherent, and the condition is affine-local on Y. Base-point-free line bundles give morphisms X → P(π_* L) (Exercise 17.3.E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative ampleness (π-ample)
rubrics_metrics.description: L is π-ample if for every affine open Spec B ⊂ Y, L|_{π^{-1}(Spec B)} is ample on π^{-1}(Spec B) over B (equivalently, absolutely ample on the fiber).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If L is ample then π is quasicompact and separated; if π is affine all invertible sheaves are ample; if π is projective the corresponding O(1) is ample. Many standard statements about ampleness carry over; see Theorem 17.3.9 for equivalent formulations under quasicompact hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorem 17.3.9 — equivalent characterizations of relative ampleness
rubrics_metrics.description: For π: X → Y proper with Y quasicompact and L invertible on X, the following are equivalent: (a) some L^{⊗N} is π-very ample; (b) for all finite-type quasicoherent F there exists n0 so that for n≥n0, L^{⊗n} ⊗ F is relatively globally generated; (c) L is π-ample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Theorem 16.6.2 in the proofs (Exercise 17.3.F). Variants removing quasicompactness on Y are possible with adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent definition of very ampleness under Noetherian hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is proper and Y is locally Noetherian (and π_* L is finite type), then L is very ample iff (i) L is relatively base-point-free, and (ii) the canonical Y-morphism i: X → P(π_* L) is a closed embedding (Exercise 17.3.G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequence: under these hypotheses relative very ampleness is affine-local on Y. The criterion reduces checking very ampleness to base-point-freeness plus embedding property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projectivization PF = Proj Sym• F and projective bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite-type quasicoherent F, Proj(Sym• F) is called the projectivization P_F; if F is locally free rank n+1 this is a P^n-bundle. P^n_X = P(O_X^{⊕n+1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projectivization behaves well under base change. Twisting by an invertible sheaf L changes O(1) accordingly (Exercise 17.2.G); e.g., P(V) ≃ P(V ⊗ L) with O(1) twisted by L.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ample vector bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: A locally free sheaf E on a proper A-scheme X is ample (as a vector bundle) if O_{P(E)/X}(1) is an ample invertible sheaf on P(E).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notion coincides with the usual ampleness for line bundles when rank=1. Properness hypotheses can be relaxed but are included to match Deﬁnition 16.6.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiaffine schemes and quasiaffine morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: X is quasiaffine if it admits a quasicompact open embedding into an affine scheme, equivalently the canonical map X → Spec Γ(X, OX) is a quasicompact open embedding. A morphism π: X → Y is quasiaffine if preimages of affine opens are quasiaffine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quasiaffine implies quasicompact and separated; notion is local on the target and preserved under base change and composition. Use Exercise 17.3.H for explicit criteria and proofs.
